locations.title: Vaskhold
locations.description: Seat of the Thane-moot.
locations.scene_headline: The moot does not seat strangers.
locations.scene_body: Thanes argue in a language of precedent older than the Ring itself.
locations.sealed_reason: The moot does not seat strangers.

locations.title: Fetterstone
locations.description: Holds prisoners Aldermere wants returned.

locations.title: The Bone Orchard
locations.description: Where oathbreakers hang, and are mourned.

locations.title: Hjarnmoot
locations.description: The oath circle. Nobody fights in it.
locations.scene_body: An oath spoken on the flat stone is as binding here as blood on the sand is at home.
locations.sealed_reason: An oath must be spoken for you first.

locations.title: Skarrow Longhall
locations.description: Hospitality is law under this roof.
locations.scene_body: Under this roof hospitality is law, which means Hjalvar Skarrow cannot harm you and cannot let you leave.
locations.sealed_reason: You have not been invited in.

locations.title: Grimsdal Mine
locations.description: Iron. Sold south without much asking.

locations.title: The Rimegate
locations.description: The pass. Everything north begins here.
locations.scene_headline: The pass is watched from both sides.
locations.scene_body: Beyond it, no one settles anything with a sword, and they find your country obscene for doing so.

locations.title: Coldwatch Tower
locations.description: Watches the northern road. Undermanned.

locations.title: The Weeping Quarry
locations.description: The Ring’s marble, cut by the sentenced.

locations.title: Thornhollow
locations.description: Not bandits. Plaintiffs, with a court of their own.
locations.scene_body: A court sits under the thorn palisade, and it has been waiting nine years for someone to bring them a seal.
locations.sealed_reason: You would have to be brought there.

locations.title: Ravensgate Bridge
locations.description: A toll the Court pretends not to know about.
locations.scene_body: Thornhollow taxes this crossing, and the Court has decided not to notice.

locations.title: Harrowfield
locations.description: A village a rigged Verdict emptied.

locations.title: Greywither Abbey
locations.description: Its cellar holds the Verdict rolls.
locations.scene_headline: The roof is gone. The cellar is not.
locations.scene_body: Sister Mave has kept the Verdict rolls dry through two winters and one fire.
locations.sealed_reason: Sister Mave opens for no one unannounced.

locations.title: The Sable Court
locations.description: No weapons. Worse dangers.
locations.scene_headline: Marble, and no weapons at all.
locations.scene_body: Every person here is measuring what your arrival costs them.
locations.sealed_reason: You have no name the Court must answer.

locations.title: The Sundial Market
locations.description: A new lead waits among the lantern stalls.
locations.scene_body: Nara Voss is already holding out her hand for the writ you have not shown her.
locations.sealed_reason: You have no reason to go there yet.

locations.title: The Chainhouse
locations.description: Cassian is not a prisoner, and cannot leave.
locations.scene_headline: The door locks from the outside.
locations.scene_body: Cassian is not a prisoner. He simply cannot leave, and the difference has stopped mattering to him.
locations.sealed_reason: Cassian’s trust will open this door.

locations.title: The Verdict Ring
locations.description: Law is made here, and it cannot be appealed.
locations.scene_body: Two champions stand on the raked sand. Whatever is decided here becomes law, and cannot be appealed.

locations.title: The Drowned Stair
locations.description: The one road out that cannot be searched.
locations.scene_headline: The water has not moved in years.
locations.scene_body: This is where the losers go. It is also the only road out that Marblegate cannot search.
locations.sealed_reason: The grate is chained from the inside.

locations.title: The Iron Fane
locations.description: It certifies every Verdict. It certified this one.
locations.scene_body: An iron ring hangs above the altar. Every Verdict for a century was certified beneath it.
locations.sealed_reason: The doors open for judgements, not for you.

locations.title: Hollowforge
locations.description: The smith arms the Ring, and quietly arms its enemies.
locations.scene_headline: The forge has not gone cold in forty years.
locations.scene_body: Hob Cardew arms the Ring. He also arms the people the Ring made homeless, and knows exactly what that makes him.
locations.sealed_reason: Hob Cardew works for the Ring, not for strangers.

locations.title: Marblegate
locations.description: Nothing leaves the city unread.
locations.scene_body: A clerk turns every page of every ledger that passes under the arch. Yours is in your coat.
locations.sealed_reason: You are carrying nothing worth the search.

locations.title: The Ferryman’s Post
locations.description: He carries every faction and judges none.

locations.title: Blackreach Hold
locations.description: The keep of whoever signed the writ.
locations.scene_body: Somewhere behind that wall is the hand that signed a Verdict before the fight.

locations.title: The Hundred Docks
locations.description: Everything arrives here, and everything is priced.
locations.scene_headline: Everything arrives, and everything is priced.
locations.scene_body: Including, it turns out, a succession.
locations.sealed_reason: You need a hull willing to carry you.

locations.title: The Debtors’ Terrace
locations.description: Where people who lost are displayed.

locations.title: The Gilt Exchange
locations.description: Judgements are listed here like cargo.
locations.scene_body: Somewhere on this floor, the verdict that will decide Aldermere has a number beside it.
locations.sealed_reason: The floor is closed to those without standing.

locations.title: The Spice Vaults
locations.description: Bonded warehouses, and a way under them.

locations.title: Casa Verrine
locations.description: The house that bought the succession.
locations.scene_headline: Lemon trees, and a strongroom door.
locations.scene_body: Aurel Verrine does not consider what he did a crime. He considers it an entry.

locations.title: The Whisper Baths
locations.description: The real deals, unclothed and unarmed.
locations.scene_body: No one here carries a weapon, which is why the real deals are made in the water.
locations.sealed_reason: You are not yet worth talking to.

locations.title: Cheira Isle
locations.description: Quarantine. Nobody checks who is on it.

choices.label: Watch the Verdict
choices.summary: Witnessed a Verdict in the Ring. The loser was carried down the stair.

memory.text: The player witnessed a Verdict in the Ring. Cassian Vale won, and the loser was carried down toward the Drowned Stair. The Sundial Market opened as the next lead.
memory.terms: Verdict, Ring, Cassian, sealed writ, market

choices.label: Go to Cassian
choices.summary: Cassian trusted the player and opened the Chainhouse and the forge.

memory.text: Cassian Vale trusted the player after the Verdict and showed a way into the Chainhouse. He is not a prisoner and cannot leave.

choices.label: Show Nara the writ
choices.summary: Nara read the sealed writ. The succession Verdict was dated before the fight.

memory.text: Nara Voss read the sealed writ in the Sundial Market. The succession Verdict is dated before the fight it decides, which means the outcome was bought.
memory.terms: writ, succession, forged date, Nara, Marblegate

choices.label: Carry it through the gate
choices.summary: The writ left Corvane. The northern road opened.

memory.text: The player carried the sealed writ out through Marblegate. Nothing leaves Corvane unread, so someone now knows it is gone.

choices.label: Put the seal before their court
choices.summary: Thornhollow recognised the seal. It took their land nine years ago.

memory.text: Thornhollow’s court recognised the seal on the writ: it is the same one that took Harrowfield nine years ago. They are not bandits but plaintiffs, and they want the writ made public.
memory.terms: Thornhollow, Iselle, Harrowfield, rigged Verdict, seal

choices.label: Ask how a thing leaves Corvane
choices.summary: Cassian described the flooded stair beneath the Ring, and the door at the far end of it.

memory.text: Cassian Vale described a flooded stair under the Verdict Ring that comes out past the wall. Nothing carried down it is ever read by a clerk.
memory.terms: drowned stair, flooded, under the wall, unsearched

choices.label: Go down and under the wall
choices.summary: The player left Corvane by the drowned stair, carrying a sealed judgement no clerk ever turned.

memory.text: The player walked out of Corvane under the wall with the sealed writ, and no gate clerk ever saw it.
memory.terms: unsearched, under the wall, carried out

choices.label: Swear a challenge on the sand
choices.summary: The player swore a challenge to a sealed Verdict, which only the Iron Fane may hear.

memory.text: The player swore a formal challenge to a Verdict in the Ring. Only the Iron Fane can hear such a thing, and it now must.

choices.label: Ask who keeps the rolls
choices.summary: Vell named Greywither Abbey as the house that has kept every Verdict roll for a century.

memory.text: Arbiter Vell said Greywither Abbey holds the Verdict rolls, and has for a hundred years.

choices.label: Say the date aloud before the Arbiter
choices.summary: The player read the writ’s date into the Fane, and the Sable Court sent for them the same day.

memory.text: The player said the writ’s date aloud inside the Iron Fane. The Sable Court sent for them before the day was out.

choices.label: Ask the Court for leave to read
choices.summary: The Sable Court granted leave to open the Greywither rolls, expecting the player to find nothing.

memory.text: The Sable Court gave the player leave to read the Greywither rolls. They granted it easily, which was itself worth noticing.
memory.terms: leave to read, rolls, court order

choices.label: Find whose hand set the seal
choices.summary: The rolls named the hand behind the seal, and named where that hand keeps its accounts.

memory.text: The Greywither rolls named the hand that set the seal on the writ, and pointed at Blackreach Hold where its accounts are kept.

choices.label: Pay for a night crossing
choices.summary: The ferryman put the player across to Blackreach Hold in the dark, and did not wait.

memory.text: A ferryman crossed the player to Blackreach Hold at night for coin, and refused to wait on the far bank.

choices.label: Ask what lies past the gate
choices.summary: The gate wardens named Vaskir and its thane-moot, and what the moot thinks of Aldermere seals.

memory.text: Past the Rimegate lies Vaskir, ruled by a thane-moot that does not recognise an Aldermere seal.

choices.label: Stand a shift with Brynn’s people
choices.summary: The player worked a shift underground, and Skarrow’s hall opened to them because of it.

memory.text: The player stood a full shift in the Grimsdal mine alongside Brynn Skarrow’s people. In Vaskir that is how a stranger becomes a guest.

choices.label: Ask Hjalvar to speak for you
choices.summary: Hjalvar Skarrow agreed to stand sponsor, which is the only way a stranger is seated at the moot.

memory.text: Hjalvar Skarrow agreed to sponsor the player before the thane-moot. His daughter Brynn vouched for them first.

choices.label: Read what the Hold was paid
choices.summary: Blackreach’s ledgers were settled in Serevane coin, from a house across the water.

memory.text: Blackreach Hold’s ledgers were paid in Serevane coin. The money behind the fixed Verdict came from across the water.

choices.label: Take ship across the water
choices.summary: The player crossed to Serevane, where the money that bought the Verdict actually lives.

memory.text: The player took ship from Blackreach to Serevane, following the money that paid for the Verdict.

choices.label: Ask whose paper this is
choices.summary: The Exchange named House Verrine without hesitation, and charged for saying it.

memory.text: The Gilt Exchange named House Verrine as the paper behind the Blackreach ledgers, and took a fee for the answer.

choices.label: Buy an introduction
choices.summary: A vault factor sold the player an hour of Aurel Verrine’s afternoon.

memory.text: The player bought an introduction to Aurel Verrine from a factor in the spice vaults. In Serevane an audience is a commodity like any other.

choices.label: Accept the invitation to the baths
choices.summary: Verrine moved the conversation to the Whisper Baths, where nothing said is ever written down.

memory.text: Aurel Verrine invited the player to the Whisper Baths. Nothing said there is written down, which is why business is done there.

choices.label: Sell the writ to Verrine
choices.summary: The player sold the sealed writ to House Verrine. The succession passed as written, and Cassian Vale died on the sand keeping the date honest.

memory.text: The player sold the sealed writ to Aurel Verrine for coin and protection. The fixed succession stood, and Cassian Vale threw the Verdict and died for it.

choices.label: Burn the writ on the Fane’s iron
choices.summary: The player destroyed the only proof the succession was fixed, and left the sand to settle it.

memory.text: The player burned the sealed writ on the iron of the Fane. The only proof the succession was arranged no longer exists.

choices.label: Put the writ in the Court’s hands
choices.summary: The Sable Court took the writ, reformed the Ring by charter, and let the succession pass without a fight.

memory.text: The player handed the sealed writ to the Sable Court. The Court reformed the Ring under a new charter rather than be caught holding it, and the succession passed bloodlessly.

choices.label: Give the writ to Thornhollow
choices.summary: Thornhollow made the writ public. A century of Verdicts is void, and the houses have gone to arms over it.

memory.text: The player gave the sealed writ to Thornhollow’s court, which read it in the open. Every Verdict of the last century is void and the houses are arming.

choices.label: Let Cassian throw the Verdict
choices.summary: The player stood in the crowd. Cassian Vale lost the succession Verdict on purpose and bled out on the sand.

memory.text: The player watched from the crowd while Cassian Vale threw the succession Verdict and died on the sand, exactly as he had been paid to.

choices.label: Fight the succession Verdict yourself
choices.summary: The player took Cassian’s place on the sand and won the succession honestly, inheriting everything it decides.

memory.text: The player fought the succession Verdict in Cassian Vale’s place and won it on the sand. The Ring stands unquestioned, and it now answers to them.
memory.terms: fought, won, succession, sand, iron verdict
